page.layout: One page of text, with two woodcut medallions above the text, each with a circular legend. Running head at top right, page number at top left. Running text in one column below the medallions. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: PELOPS Tantali regis Phrygum filius fuit,qui Hippoda-miam Pisæ regis filiam deperibat:atque in uxorem petês eam, à patre virginis elegātissimæ,Oenamao,iniquis propositis con-ditionibus,est reiectus.quæ res bellum suscitauit : Oenomaus, Myrtilo præfecto suo prodete,victus est.Pelops itaque sumpta in uxore Hippodamia,Pisæregnum tenuit,anno à mundo con-dito 2617. ante Christum natum 1346. Hic viribus ac prudentia insignis,cum plurimos in Peloponnesum accolas dedu-xisset,eam patriâ Peloponnesum ab se denominauit.Diod.lib. 5. circa finem. regnauit annis 59.in Pisa,quæ est in Elide,iuxta Archadiam,cuius incolæ eam quæ eiusdem nominis est in Italia,condidere. Vide Strabone lib. Geographiæ 7.&8.item Rapha. Volaterranum lib.34.

Hippodamia filia fuit unica,eadémque formofiffima Oeno-mai Elidis regis:hanc à multis procis ambitam , nemini voluit collocare pater:quam tamen Pelops accepit in uxore,victo patre virginis , fraude Myrtili, qui in mare præcipitatus, nomen Myrtoo mari dediffe dicitur. Hinc illa Poëtarum fabula , de Myrtilo auriga , pecunia corrupto , & de curru vitiato,& deficiente. Unde Ouidius epist.8.
Facit autem Ouid. Hermionem loquentem, quæ erat Pelopis proneptis:nam Pelops erat ei proauus.

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits: left a bearded man with a crown (legend PELOPS ... PHRYG.), right a woman with a headdress (legend HIPPODAMIA VXOR PELOPIS, the VXOR in the top arc). Transcribed the legends as printed, with V as U. The text has a few doubtful forms: "petês" and "prodete" are copied as printed and may carry accents not fully legible. "Diod.lib. 5." and "59" are spaced as printed in the scan.
